quotes.speaker: Trysta Krick
quotes.summary_phrase: Trysta Krick argues the Fire's home environment is superior to the Blazers'
quotes.excerpt: the Fire game environment is so much better than a Blazer game environment

text_blocks.speaker: Trysta Krick
text_blocks.text: The Fire game environment is so much better than a Blazer game environment. It's by a magnitude of five or ten.

text_blocks.speaker: Breanna Stewart
text_blocks.text: I honestly think that there's a level of engagement that's heightened in W games compared to NBA games.

quotes.speaker: Trysta Krick
quotes.summary_phrase: Trysta Krick believes Victor Wembanyama is reaching his peak potential
quotes.excerpt: Wemby is just coming into the peak of his powers. He's able to eat up that much paint.
quotes.quote: If the Knicks don't get it now, I don't know that they're ever going to get it. I think Wemby is just coming into the peak of his powers. You look at what he's able to do, thinking about somebody that tall, that long, being able to eat up that much paint as fast as he can and really providing a lot of protection for the guards like Steph Curry, like Dylan Harper, like even De'Aaron Fox to be ultra-aggressive on the perimeter. I feel like Wemby's only going to get better.

quotes.speaker: Breanna Stewart
quotes.summary_phrase: Breanna Stewart reflects on the Spurs' team chemistry and growth
quotes.excerpt: Spurs just wanted it more. They look like they have this team that is really young.
quotes.quote: Last night watching the Game 7, Spurs just wanted it more. They look like they have this team that is really young. They've kind of built it back from the ground up. They've gone through the trenches together and really excited for each person individually.

quotes.speaker: Breanna Stewart
quotes.summary_phrase: Breanna Stewart insists the Knicks won't lose a home playoff series
quotes.excerpt: The Knicks are not going to lose a series on their home court in the finals.
quotes.quote: The Knicks are not going to lose a series on their home court in the finals. That's not happening. My X-factor is going to be Mikal Bridges because he basically brought them back in that game.

quotes.speaker: Trysta Krick
quotes.summary_phrase: Trysta Krick highlights Portland's surprising win total this season
quotes.excerpt: Their win total was 11.5 and they already have six wins and it's not even June yet.
quotes.quote: It's got to be Portland, right? Their win total was 11.5 and they already have six wins and it's not even June yet. The people who make the odds, they say that they believe that Portland will either win 11 games or they'll win 12 games. So they set it right there in the middle. A good season is probably that they thought they put them right there with the Connecticut Sun.

quotes.speaker: Trysta Krick
quotes.summary_phrase: Trysta Krick identifies intensity as the key to Portland's success
quotes.excerpt: The key piece for this team to continue to perform is intensity.
quotes.quote: The key piece for this team to continue to perform is intensity. They're sprint speed is the highest in the league. Their deceleration speed is the highest. And so those intensity metrics are so high. I think they're number one in forced turnovers per game, number one in steals per 100 possessions per game. And my biggest question mark is like, are they going to burn the fuck out?

quotes.speaker: Trysta Krick
quotes.summary_phrase: Trysta Krick praises Megan Gustafson's emergence and defensive impact
quotes.excerpt: I thought the way that Megan Gustafson has sort of emerged... she took the task of D-ing up Alia Boston.

text_blocks.speaker: Trysta Krick
text_blocks.text: I thought the way that Megan Gustafson has sort of emerged... I saw her play in the building against Indiana. Not only was she able to catch in all angles, short roll, long roll, she took the task of D-ing up Alia Boston, which is not an easy task. She gets the start, I think that was her first start of the year, and she's eight for eight from the field. You look at Emily Engstler, who I think is leading the league right now in blocks and is top three in steals at 6'1. Just insane what she's been able to do, her and Sophie Cunningham going back and forth.

text_blocks.speaker: Breanna Stewart
text_blocks.text: Pauline is definitely kind of embracing her role and her opportunity and just being confident. We all know that she's an incredibly dynamic scorer.

quotes.speaker: Trysta Krick
quotes.summary_phrase: Trysta Krick discusses the difficulty of balancing motherhood and professional sports
quotes.excerpt: It's impressive for women who are badass doing everything in their job at a super high level.
quotes.quote: I always think about that as I've gotten older. I think about that balance and how impressive it is for women who are badass doing everything in their job at a super high level and then managing that with what is a full-time job as well.

quotes.speaker: Trysta Krick
quotes.summary_phrase: Trysta Krick argues that the WNBA should have its own dedicated schedule
quotes.excerpt: Why aren't you just putting the WNBA on its own slot on its own day like it deserves?
quotes.quote: Why aren't you just putting the WNBA on its own slot on its own day like it deserves? Why is it competing with other things?

quotes.speaker: Trysta Krick
quotes.summary_phrase: Trysta Krick shares her personal history with the Portland Trail Blazers
quotes.excerpt: My mom got me into the Blazers when I was like four or five. I was a huge Clyde Drexler fan.
quotes.quote: My mom got me into the Blazers when I was like four or five. That was in the early 90s. And so I was a huge Clyde Drexler fan. That was like my favorite player. And we moved back to Portland when I was like six or seven, and that's when I really ended up playing a lot of, I guess you could call it more organized than it was in the country of Northern California.

quotes.speaker: Trysta Krick
quotes.summary_phrase: Trysta Krick explains her transition from finance to sports media
quotes.excerpt: I ended up going into finance right out of college for like five years and hated every second.
quotes.quote: I ended up going into finance right out of college for like five years and hated every second of putting on the button-ups and the heels and the stretchy A-line skirts. None of that. I was trying to be Michelle Tafoya or Erin Andrews or whoever, and that shit did not get me anywhere. Everything was awkward, everything was uncomfortable. I was trying to be Michelle Tafoya or Erin Andrews or whoever, and like it was leaning into my hip-hop background. I was a little rapper going up, and then I was in a pencil skirt, yeah, from cornrows to like baby doll bangs.

quotes.speaker: Trysta Krick
quotes.summary_phrase: Trysta Krick predicts that Enrique and Paige will not work together
quotes.excerpt: Enrique and Paige will never work together at a high level.
quotes.quote: Enrique and Paige will never work together at a high level.

quotes.speaker: Trysta Krick
quotes.summary_phrase: Trysta Krick criticizes PR teams for providing generic game credentials
quotes.excerpt: What drives me crazy is when PR people are on some bullshit.
quotes.quote: What drives me crazy is when PR people are on some bullshit. And it's like you know I'm coming to every game and yet you still keep giving me the game-by-game credential. It's like fam, what are we doing here?

quotes.speaker: Trysta Krick
quotes.summary_phrase: Trysta Krick discusses the challenge of balancing multiple sports interests
quotes.excerpt: What drove me crazy was sitting there for fire fever and it's at the exact same time.
quotes.quote: What drove me crazy was sitting there for fire fever and it's at the exact same time as the Western Conference Finals Game 7 and I had to choose. Like that shit drives me crazy. Like don't do that. That's horrible. Don't pit us against one another.

quotes.quote: Last chance on the mic to prove that I got heat, my style's discrete, or can you like crete.
